nodes.title: Windows development checks fail in a fresh checkout
nodes.body:
### Describe the bug

A fresh Windows checkout can fail both development checks required by `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```text
go test ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
```

I hit four Windows-specific blockers while running those checks:

- With `core.autocrlf=true`, checked-out Go files use CRLF and the `gofmt` formatter reports hundreds of unchanged files as improperly formatted.
- `Test_newIOStreams_pager` inherits `GH_PAGER` and `PAGER` from the invoking shell when a test case does not set them, so an outer `GH_PAGER=cat` changes the test result.
- The Huh prompt test harness uses `io.Pipe`; the Bubble Tea forms time out instead of completing on Windows.
- The credential updater test passes an unquoted Windows temporary path with backslashes to Git's credential helper configuration. Git's shell parsing consumes the separators and writes path-shaped credential files into the repository root.

The failures are in separate test helpers, but together they prevent the documented repository-wide checks from completing on Windows.

A candidate fix is available in draft PR #14155. I am keeping it in draft pending triage and guidance on whether these fixes should stay together or be split.

### Affected version

```text
cli/cli trunk at 0eeec0b92edbe70199f9768522f831d3534f41ad
go version go1.26.6 windows/amd64
golangci-lint 2.12.2
Windows 11 (10.0.26200.0)
```

The line-ending failure was reproduced in a fresh checkout configured with `core.autocrlf=true`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On Windows, create a fresh checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`.
2. Set `GH_PAGER=cat` and `PAGER=cat` in the invoking shell.
3. Run `go test ./...`.
4. Run `golangci-lint run ./...`.
5. Inspect the repository root for untracked credential test artifacts.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected:

- The documented test and lint commands pass in a fresh Windows checkout.
- Prompt tests complete using native Windows I/O behavior.
- Credential tests keep their files inside the test temporary directory.

Actual:

- The linter reports unchanged Go files as failing `gofmt` because their worktree copies use CRLF.
- Pager assertions observe `cat` instead of the value declared by each test case.
- Huh prompt tests report `form.Run() did not complete in time`.
- Credential updater tests can leave files such as `Users...TempTestUpdate...credentials` in the repository root.

### Proposed acceptance criteria

- A fresh Windows checkout configured with `core.autocrlf=true` keeps Go worktree files in the line-ending form expected by `gofmt`.
- `go test ./...` passes when the invoking shell already defines `GH_PAGER` and `PAGER`.
- Huh prompt interaction tests complete on Windows without replacing the real Bubble Tea event loop.
- Credential updater tests support Windows paths, including paths containing spaces, and leave no artifacts in the repository root.
- `golangci-lint 2.12.2 run ./...` reports no issues in that fresh checkout.

If this scope is acceptable for an external contribution, please confirm whether #14155 should remain one PR or be split by failure mode.

### Logs

Representative failures:

```text
File is not properly formatted (gofmt)
expected: "CONFIG_PAGER"
actual  : "cat"
form.Run() did not complete in time
```

nodes.title: gh skill install --agent codex --scope user installs to the deprecated ~/.codex/skills
nodes.body:
### Summary

`gh skill install --agent codex` uses two different directory conventions depending on scope:

| scope | installs to | correct? |
|---|---|---|
| `--scope project` | `.agents/skills/` | yes |
| `--scope user` | `~/.codex/skills/` | no, should be `~/.agents/skills/` |

Project scope already follows the `.agents` convention, so the user-scope path looks like it was simply missed when the rest was updated.

### Why `~/.codex/skills` is wrong

Codex resolves skill roots in [`codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs):

```rust
const AGENTS_DIR_NAME: &str = ".agents";
const SKILLS_DIR_NAME: &str = "skills";
```

- user level resolves to `home_dir.join(AGENTS_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME)`, i.e. `~/.agents/skills`
- `$CODEX_HOME/skills` is still read, but the source comments it as *"Deprecated user skills location (`$CODEX_HOME/skills`), kept for backward compatibility"*

The Codex documentation lists only `$CWD/.agents/skills`, `$CWD/../.agents/skills`, `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills` for repositories, and `$HOME/.agents/skills` plus `/etc/codex/skills` otherwise.

So installs still work today, but only through a path Codex has marked deprecated, and they break whenever that fallback is dropped.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
gh skill install <owner>/<repo> <skill> --agent codex --scope user
ls ~/.agents/skills   # empty
ls ~/.codex/skills    # the skill is here
```

For contrast, project scope behaves correctly:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q .
gh skill install <owner>/<repo> <skill> --agent codex --scope project
# → "Installed <skill> ... in .agents\skills"
```

### Expected

User-scope Codex installs land in `~/.agents/skills`, matching the project-scope behaviour and Codex's documented lookup order.

Worth deciding separately whether `gh skill list` / `update` should keep recognising skills already installed under `~/.codex/skills`, so existing installs are not orphaned by the change.

### Versions

- `gh version 2.95.0 (2026-06-17)`
- `codex-cli 0.144.1`
- Windows 11

nodes.title: test: stabilize Windows development checks
nodes.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

Fixes #14156

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

Windows development checks had four platform-specific failure modes:

- Git's default `core.autocrlf=true` checkout converted Go files to CRLF, so the `gofmt` formatter reported hundreds of unchanged files.
- The pager test inherited `GH_PAGER` and `PAGER` from the invoking shell when a test case did not set them.
- The Huh test harness used `io.Pipe`, which prevented Bubble Tea forms from completing on Windows.
- The credential updater test passed an unquoted Windows path with backslashes to Git's credential helper configuration, causing Git to write test credentials into the repository root.

This change pins Go files to LF in `.gitattributes`, isolates pager environment variables, uses an OS pipe for the Huh event loop, and quotes a slash-normalized temporary credential path.

The changes affect development and test behavior only. Production `gh` behavior is unchanged.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Show how you exercised the change yourself, as a user of `gh` would.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios. For example:
   Given I am in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I run `gh pr list`
   Then I see "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

On Windows with Git's global `core.autocrlf=true`, I checked out the committed branch into a fresh worktree and inspected representative Go files with `git ls-files --eol`. Their index and worktree forms were both LF, and the repository-wide linter no longer proposed formatter changes.

I kept `GH_PAGER=cat` and `PAGER=cat` in the outer shell while exercising the full test suite. The pager cases used their own declared environments, the Huh form interactions completed, and the credential updater left its file in the temporary directory instead of creating path-shaped files in the repository root.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- The LF rule is limited to `*.go`; this avoids changing line-ending policy for unrelated file types.
- The PR does not contain a bulk line-ending rewrite. Renormalizing the index changed only the four intended files.
- `os.Pipe` preserves the real Bubble Tea event-loop coverage while providing a native cross-platform pipe.
- Converting the temporary credential path to slash form before quoting supports Windows drive paths and paths containing spaces.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with `.gitattributes` and `internal/prompter/huh_prompter_test.go`; those address the two failures that prevented repository-wide Windows checks from completing. The pager and credential changes isolate the remaining test-only leaks discovered by that run.
